entradas.text: It was early evening, still light out with just a faint nip in the air. Franc was at a friend's and Deana was at an art class. Monica and I decided to go out for a walk before dinner.
Monica met me by the door, and we put on our coats and hats.
“One way or another, I want to contribute to this country. No matter what happens.”
Monica beamed at me, her face flush with excitement.
“Let’s get back to the house for dinner."
What did our ideals really mean if they could be changed so easily? What about the people we idolize?
Ionas had once fought hard and strong against Soll’s judiciary reforms. But after years of the government blocking his every move, he gave up on his ideals and became a part of the administration.

As we reached the river, we saw Ionas Crona, the former Minister of Justice, walking in the opposite direction. I remembered that Nia Morgna used to be his Vice Minister. He gave us a quick nod of acknowledgement.
This was why I had married her -- this passion and resolve. I should have anticipated that, sooner or later, she would join me in the political arena.
“Otherwise, we will end up like...”
“We are not weak, Anton. But we are only strong as long as we stand by our ideals. ”
“Ewald Alphonso?”
entradas.menu: “Ewald Alphonso?”

entradas.text: “Colonel Soll?”
entradas.menu: “Colonel Soll?”

entradas.text: “Ionas Crona?”
entradas.menu: “Ionas Crona?”

entradas.text: “Our former president tried his best. Yes, he failed, but his ideals weren't the reason."
“Take another guess.”
“Guess again.”
“Say what you will, but that relic of the past was and frankly still is one of the most idealistic people in Sordland."
“Exactly. He backed down on his ideals and now everyone knows him for what he actually is...”
At that moment, we passed Ionas Crona again. He was on a nearby bench, taking a smoke break after his own walk. Monica plastered on a big smile and greeted him, then turned back to me.
“...Spineless.”
We rose from the bench and started making our way back home.
If that was how people remembered Ionas, how would they remember me? Whatever he had done, whatever ideals he had lost, he must have had his reasons.
Would they remember me as a true patriot? A reformer of the country? What would they write about me in the history books?
“Of course. Lead the way.”
entradas.menu: “Of course. Lead the way.”

entradas.text: I was just starting to understand the meaning of those words.
The sun began to set over the horizon, bathing the clouds in shades of orange and pink.
“So, how was your day?”
“Paperwork, endless meetings... the usual nightmare.”
entradas.menu: “Paperwork, endless meetings... the usual nightmare.”

entradas.text: “I'd rather not say.”
entradas.menu: “I'd rather not say.”

entradas.text: “How was yours?”
entradas.menu: “How was yours?”

entradas.text: “That good, was it?”
"I don't know. I imagine some might find that stimulating."
"Avoiding my question, are we? Very well.”
“What about your day?"
entradas.menu: “What about your day?"

entradas.text: “Oh, it was fine. I caught up on some reading while the children were at school.”
"Evelyn also came round for tea. She says hi. She was feeling rather low, though. Apparently she and Petr had a bit of a disagreement."
“Apparently Petr had too much whiskey -- as usual -- and didn't behave when Evelyn's father was over for dinner yesterday.”
“I hope so. They always seemed so close.”
“That's Petr -- perpetually pickled. I'll have a talk with him.”
entradas.menu: “That's Petr -- perpetually pickled. I'll have a talk with him.”

entradas.text: “It's just a rough patch, love. They'll be fine."
entradas.menu: “It's just a rough patch, love. They'll be fine."

entradas.text: “To be honest, I don't care."
entradas.menu: “To be honest, I don't care."

entradas.text: “Who?”
entradas.menu: “Who?”

entradas.text: “Oh, Janice... Right.”
entradas.menu: “Oh, Janice... Right.”

entradas.text: “You remember, my friend from university? We were in the Sordish Literature class together?"
Neither the name nor the description rang a bell.
“Anyway, she's been working as an executive assistant at the Violet Pictures film studio."
“Right, right, that Janice."
entradas.menu: “Right, right, that Janice."

entradas.text: “I still don't remember her, but go on."
entradas.menu: “I still don't remember her, but go on."

entradas.text: "She recently became pregnant, and asked her boss for paid maternity leave. And guess what?"
“She was fired for it!”
“After asking for maternity leave? That's terrible.”
entradas.menu: “After asking for maternity leave? That's terrible.”

entradas.text: “So what?”
entradas.menu: “So what?”

entradas.text: “I know, I was beside myself when she told me. And that's not all.”
“They immediately replaced her with a younger, less experienced man -- the son of an executive, no less.“
“So what? She was sobbing, Anton. I asked her about what happened afterwards.”
“That is utterly ridiculous.”
entradas.menu: “That is utterly ridiculous.”

entradas.text: “So she called the First Lady to ask for help?"
entradas.menu: “So she called the First Lady to ask for help?"

entradas.text: "Nepotism, eh? They must have wanted him in there all along."
entradas.menu: "Nepotism, eh? They must have wanted him in there all along."

entradas.text: “I'm happy you agree with me."
“She called a friend. She knows this is something I'm passionate about.“
"That doesn't justify what they did to her."
“As it happens, another friend works for a television station that's hiring secretaries, so I connected the two of them.“
"Terrific! Problem solved, then."
entradas.menu: "Terrific! Problem solved, then."

entradas.text: “That doesn't solve the deeper problem, though."
entradas.menu: “That doesn't solve the deeper problem, though."

entradas.text: “I know that the mayor of Anrica, Curtan Leste, will be delivering a speech at the annual opening of the Benfi festival.“
“I want our voice heard, and this festival is the time to do it. I just need your blessing as my husband and the President of Sordland.“
“You have my full support. Always.”
entradas.menu: “You have my full support. Always.”

entradas.text: “Absolutely not. Out of the question.”
entradas.menu: “Absolutely not. Out of the question.”

entradas.text: “Sure, it's just a speech. What's the worst that can happen?”
entradas.menu: “Sure, it's just a speech. What's the worst that can happen?”

entradas.text: “I don't want you to step into politics.”
entradas.menu: “I don't want you to step into politics.”

entradas.text: “It's not the right time. Sordland is facing too much political strife -- we'll have to deal with women's rights later.”
entradas.menu: “It's not the right time. Sordland is facing too much political strife -- we'll have to deal with women's rights later.”

entradas.text: "This is why I love you. Thank you, Anton -- you have no idea how much this means to me."
"I won't let you down, Anton. Thank you.“
Monica was silent for a while. When she finally spoke, there was a chill in her voice.
“If that's truly how you feel, so be it."
We walked back home, neither of us looking at the other.
“Sorry, but I can't make Curtan Leste angry."
entradas.menu: “Sorry, but I can't make Curtan Leste angry."

entradas.text: “What little trouble this causes in the short term is nothing compared to the lasting, positive change it will bring -- not just for women, but for all of Sordland."
"All right. If it means so much to you, I'll make the arrangements for you to speak.”
entradas.menu: "All right. If it means so much to you.,I'll make the arrangements for you to speak."

entradas.text: “I don't think so.”
entradas.menu: “I don't think so.”

entradas.text: “My wish is to take his place and deliver the speech instead."
“It's not just a speech -- it's an opportunity for real change. An end to centuries of oppression, and the beginning of a more equal society.“
“I don't understand. Isn't this something you care about as well?"
"Women in this country are still seen as wives and mothers first, human beings second.”
“I know I'm not experienced. But I can do this. You have to trust me!“
“My word is final. You will not make the speech.”
entradas.menu: “My word is final. You will not do the speech.”

entradas.text: “I want to base the speech on women's rights in Sordland. On the oppression and discrimination we face everyday, on the basis of our sex alone."
Monica's eyes were blazing with a fire I hadn't seen since we were students. She wanted this badly.
But I had to be careful with my promises.
"I hope yours was better?"
entradas.menu: "I hope yours was better?"

entradas.text: “You know Petr. What do you think of this?”
“Good. Evelyn seemed close to tears.”
“Maybe you should. He's your vice president after all. And they're our closest friends.”
"A few years younger than me, red hair, scar on her forehead? We had dinner with her and her husband once or twice."
“But she's been working there for years without so much as a raise. Something is wrong with this, Anton. And that's not all.”
"Of course. I'll lead the way."
entradas.menu: Lead the way yourself.

entradas.text: “What's she nagging him about this time?"
entradas.menu: “What's she nagging him about this time?"

entradas.text: “You know Evelyn hasn't been the same since what happened to her at Holsord Post last year.”
“You remember -- how she got fired for supporting Alphonso? Petr tried everything to get her job back, but it didn't work.”
“Petr's in the doghouse again? How'd it happen?”
entradas.menu: “Petr's in the doghouse again? How'd it happen?”

entradas.text: "But enough about the Vecterns. I also spoke to Janice on the phone."
“Maybe he didn't try hard enough.”
entradas.menu: “Maybe he didn't try hard enough.”

entradas.text: “She had it coming.”
entradas.menu: “She had it coming.”

entradas.text: “A sad day for journalism and free speech in Sordland.”
entradas.menu: “A sad day for journalism and free speech in Sordland.”

entradas.text: "How can you say that? It was a sad day for freedom of the press in Sordland."
“I don't think anything would have worked. It was a sad day for freedom of the press in Sordland.”
“I completely agree. A sad day indeed.”
“Look at it from a cost standpoint. Obviously, they don't want to lose money.”
entradas.menu: “Look at it from a cost standpoint. Obviously, they don't want to lose money.”

entradas.text: I kept walking.
entradas.menu: Keep walking in silence.

entradas.text: “They're harassed at work, underpaid, blocked from positions of power... and those are the lucky ones!"
“The fact that there are still places in this country where little girls like Deana are denied the right to an education--”
“Go on.”
entradas.menu: “Go on.”

entradas.text: “I'm sure the parents have their reasons.”
entradas.menu: “I'm sure the parents have their reasons.”

entradas.text: “Yes, and I will do what I can to change that.“
entradas.menu: “Yes, and I will do what I can to change that.“

entradas.text: “What kind of reasons, Anton? What could justify this?"
“Poverty.”
entradas.menu: “Poverty.”

entradas.text: “Tradition.”
entradas.menu: “Tradition.”

entradas.text: “Then more work must be done to grant everyone an affordable education. And in the meantime, these girls and women like Janice need someone to speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman."
“These backwards ideals are slowing down Sordland's transformation into a modern nation.”
“These little girls and people like Janice need to have someone who can speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman.“
“Which brings me to my point.“
“These little girls and people like Janice need someone to speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman.“
"It can't just be you. These little girls and people like Janice need someone to speak on their behalf. A role model. A successful woman.“
“Nonsense. We have our guards -- there's nothing to be afraid of. Let's go to Capitol Park.”
entradas.menu: “Nonsense. We have our guards -- there's nothing to be afraid of. Let's go to Capitol Park.”

entradas.text: “I was going to suggest we walk towards Soll Square, but the guards told me it's been closed for yet another protest.”
“I wonder who they are protesting this time.”
“What does it matter? They are two sides of the same coin.”
entradas.menu: “What does it matter? They are two sides of the same coin.”

entradas.text: “Common thugs. I will make sure they are punished.”
entradas.menu: “Common thugs. I will make sure they are punished.”

entradas.text: “Must be those damn communists again.”
entradas.menu: “Must be those damn communists again.”

entradas.text: “The Young Sords are taking it too far.”
entradas.menu: “The Young Sords are taking it too far.”

entradas.text: “In any case, where shall we go? I'm not sure Capitol Park is a wise idea in this climate, either...
“You're right -- it's not worth the security risk. Let's stay inside the green perimeter.”
entradas.menu: “You're right -- it's not worth the security risk. Let's stay inside the green perimeter.”

entradas.text: Our favorite place for a stroll was the nearby Capitol Park, the largest green space in all of Holsord. Before the children were born, we had spent many an evening engaged in deep conversation along the riverside promenade.

Another favored path wound through the woods behind the presidential housing complex, to a private pond where the children could swim in summer. I was told that Soll himself had it built. The benefits of being president.
“All right. Let's go, then, before the children get home.”
“I agree. Let's go, then, before the children get home.”
I informed the guards about our route and we left the house.
I informed the guards about our route and we left the house.
The guards followed us with a black Kadilla as we exited the gates. Walking briskly, we reached Capitol Park in minutes.
The guards followed at a discreet distance as we headed towards the walking trail.
As we entered the woods, Monica broke the silence.
As we entered the park, Monica broke the silence.
“I was going to suggest we walk towards Soll Square, but the guards told me it's been closed because of the emergency act.”
“There are so many police officers in the city now, it's starting to remind me of the twenties.”
“I wonder how long this will go on.”
“They're protecting us against our enemies.”
entradas.menu: “They're protecting us against our enemies.”

entradas.text: “As long as it has to.”
entradas.menu: “As long as it has to.”

entradas.text: “I understand.”
“So you say. But I still don't like seeing so many guns on the streets.”
“I know. It's unnerving to me too.”
entradas.menu: “I know. It's unnerving to me too.”

entradas.text: “Let's hope it has an effect and the threat subsides.”

Leste was one of Sordland's most influential politicians. He had started his career in Benfi before rising to power in Anrica. Benfi's current mayor had personally invited him to make the opening speech.
Replacing him with Monica would likely anger him -- probably not enough to cause a huge incident, but enough that he might use his influence over the conservatives to block me in the Assembly.
When we arrived home, I called my secretary Livia and asked her to inform Mr. Leste that Monica would be making the speech in his stead.
"You were a damn communist yourself, once upon a time."
"You were one of those thugs yourself, once upon a time."
"You didn't think that when you were a Young Sord yourself."
"This is different. A nastier breed."
entradas.menu: "This is different. A nastier breed."

entradas.text: "I was young and stupid. I didn't know any better."
entradas.menu: "I was young and stupid. I didn't know any better."

entradas.text: "Old grudges die hard, I see."
"The Anton I knew in university never would have said that."
"You always did believe yourself to be above the fray."
"Funny how becoming president changes one's perspective."
entradas.menu: "Funny how becoming president changes one's perspective."

entradas.text: "Aren't you glad you and I don't have these kinds of quarrels?"
entradas.menu: "Aren't you glad you and I don't have these kinds of quarrels?"

entradas.text: "Being married to a shrew like her would make anyone turn to the bottle."
entradas.menu: "Being married to a shrew like her would make anyone turn to the bottle."

entradas.text: Monica gave me a quick kiss on the cheek. We continued walking.
Monica didn't say anything. We kept walking.
Monica gave me a sharp look. We kept walking.
“Can't her husband provide for the both of them while she raises the child?"
entradas.menu: “Can't her husband provide for the both of them while she raises the child?"

entradas.text: “But why should she have to lose her job? Something is wrong with this, Anton. And that's not all."
"So you're finally starting to see things my way!"
"Exactly! I knew you'd be on the same page."
"You still don't understand, do you?"
"Really, Anton? After everything we've talked about?"
We were right in front of one of the park benches that lined the river. Monica gestured to it, and we sat down.
We had reached the pond at the end of the trail. A park bench overlooked the water. Monica gestured to it, and we sat down.
“Does it have to be at the festival? Why can't you make your speech another time?"
entradas.menu: “Does it have to be at the festival? Why can't you make your speech another time?"

entradas.text: “I don't understand. After all I've done to support you, you can't support me on this?"
“Women belong in the home, not in politics."
entradas.menu: “Women belong in the home, not in politics."

entradas.text: “It has to be now. Thousands go to this festival, and millions watch the speeches at home. Sordland's women can't wait any longer!“

Just outside the gate, I glimpsed Ionas Crona, the former Minister of Justice, walking towards Capitol Park. I remembered that Nia Morgna used to be his Vice Minister. He didn't seem to notice us as he walked by.
Monica smiled.
"You know, I believe I will."
"For a good reason."
entradas.menu: "For a good reason."

entradas.text: It was early evening, still light out with just a faint nip in the air. Franc was at a friend's and Deana was at an art class. Monica and I decided to go out for a walk before dinner.
It was early evening, still light out with just a faint nip in the air. Franc was at a friend's and Deana was at an art class. Monica and I decided to go out for a walk before dinner.
“Remember my time with the Sordish League of Women in university? You supported me then. I'm asking you to support me now.“
"Serge said he found something in the car after bringing it up from the garage."
"A letter. Hand-folded, no envelope. Just the initials E.M. on the corner."
"How’d it get there?"
"That's unusual."
"That’s the thing. He swore no one’s been near the car since last night."
"But he passed it on after I read it, and the Presidential Guard took it -- standard protocol -- apparently. They check for poison, residue, that sort of thing."
"Someone got close enough to leave a note in my car?"
"You read it first? What did it say?"
"Probably just someone trying to mess with us."
"Should’ve let them take it before you opened it."
"I only remember parts... but they’re hard to forget."
"Maybe."
"I know. I hesitated. But it was already open."
"I didn’t get far before passing it on, but enough."
"The Palace was built on lies... from the beginning. Not by the divine, nor the people, but by intent."
"I have borne the same burden. I only understood when it came for E.A."
"And then something cryptic: ‘Burn the old. Through fire, the new can be born. Until then, an interregnum will bring pain... and the prairie will strangle itself.’"
"Let the Guard finish their sweep. I will check on it sometime."
"E.M. knew too much. If they got that close, they could be watching everything."
"Maybe they’re warning me. Or warning me off."
"Already asked. They’ll send it if it clears."
"That’s what I thought. It didn’t sound like a threat. It sounded like regret."
"I’ve been thinking the same. That letter wasn’t intercepted... it was delivered."
"Maybe it’s just some bored revolutionary kid, trying to sound important."
"Maybe. But if it was a joke, it was a sharp one."
"Anyway, we should enjoy the run. It's one of the few things we have just for *us*"
We jogged on for a few quiet minutes.
A sleek cat leapt across the path ahead of us. Silver fur, one blue eye, one green, an Agn cat, no doubt. After a brief look it then disappeared into a hedge with a flick of its marbled tail.
"I had two like that when I was young. My mother raised them. They used to nap in the windows all day and vanish at night like little ghosts."
"I always thought you looked most at peace when you talked about that house."
"I remember you told me one used to sit on your piano stool while you practiced... like it was judging your technique."
"I don’t think I ever had a place like that. Maybe that’s why I never learned how to miss it."
"Then we’ll make one. No matter what happens around us, we still can. And if not for us, for the kids."
"It did. Even when things were tense... there was still breath in it. Like it was holding space for us."
"He was merciless. Always left the room when I hit the wrong notes."
"Together. That’s all that matters in the end."
"The past is the past. We have a great future to look forward to. One that we can build."
